statement.p: For the function F(t) = e^{t^{2}}, let f(t) = F'(t). Write the integral \int_a^b\,f(t)\,dt and evaluate it with the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.

p.em: (Note that your answer must be exact, not a decimal approximation.)

static.solution: f(t) = F'(t), so the integral we want is \int_{0}^{4}\,e^{t^{2}}\cdot 2t\,dt. We can evaluate this with the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, and have \int_{0}^{4}\,e^{t^{2}}\cdot 2t\,dt = e^{4^{2}} - e^{0^{2}}.
